title: Go Ahead And Like What You See

contact_edits.before: The classroom provides the most drama, the most comedy, and -- whatever your background or gender -- the sharpest recognition. These primary-school kids seem to have the same teacher in every grade, a Miss Campbell, a sentimental battleaxe with a revisionist view of the Massacre of Glencoe, the 1692 atrocity in which, with encouragement from the English, the Campbell clan slaughtered the MacDonald clan in their beds. Literally, as the MacDonalds were their guests at the time. Miss Campbell, true to her family pride, believes that her ancestors have been much misjudged, and that the MacDonalds, always a shifty race, had it coming. My own observation is that the mutual suspicion may well persist to this day, between those who love soup and those who love burgers. As luck would have it, there is a David MacDonald in the class who, with his runny nose and attention deficit, reminds Elsa, who is nonetheless his only protector, of a troll. The show's finest scene is a singing contest at which the rich bitchette acquits herself atrociously, the despised David huskily but truly, Elsa herself outlandishly with windmill gestures and Adelle, tastefully disregarding all the direction Elsa has tried to give her, quite beautifully. Miss Campbell renders true judgment, thereby overcoming all her prejudices, except the unshakable one in favour of the poetry of Robert Burns. (Elsa's feelings about her friend's success are, not surprisingly, mixed, and drive her temporarily into the arms of the snobs.) Singing badly when you can sing well is really hard but Ardal -- without accompaniment, mind you -- makes all four vocal performances completely convincing and melts us with the last as surely as Adelle melts Miss Campbell. It's the crown of a virtuoso performance. She has every right to fancy herself. - You Fancy Yourself is at Theatre Passe Muraille Backspace until Feb. 14. Call 416-504-7529 for tickets and information.
